ontology.note: The semantic contract belongs to the ruleset, which declares its own output vocabulary and basis; do not infer one from this widget.

changes.description: Two comparisons for text: has an item starting with any of (`startsWith`), and has no item starting with any of (`notStartsWith`). An item is each part of the text between semicolons, slashes, ampersands or spaces, so a discharge diagnosis written J10.1;R50.9 is two codes, and J10 starts the first. That is how ESSENCE reads a code written ^[;/ ]J10^ in NSSP's syndrome definitions, with the ampersand added for ICD-11's clusters. Evaluated directly, like contains.
A word in double quotes keeps its spaces. " flu " finds stomach flu and not influenza, as NSSP's ^ flu ^ does; without the quotes it was trimmed to flu, which influenza contains.

Reading a published ruleset in the rule editor took any column compared by anything other than equals for a number, so a ruleset of words showed its text column as a number. A word comparison now means text.
Its Inspector, its dialogs and the rule list moved out of app.ts into src/ruleset-ui.ts, unchanged in what they do.

evidence.note:

That is evidence about the rulesets and about this widget's four stages; it does not certify the widget independently, and it says nothing about whether any threshold is right. 0.12.0: tests/seven-one-seven.browser.mjs (four cases by hand: 9 and -1 days, NoVerdict where onset or response is missing); Chromium.
